title: Tink AEAD, Associated Data, and Envelope Design Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies tink aead, associated data, and envelope design?
options: Use a reviewed AEAD primitive and bind ciphertext to stable, visible, canonical context through associated data.
Put the access token in associated data
Return empty plaintext when authentication fails
questions.answer: Use a reviewed AEAD primitive and bind ciphertext to stable, visible, canonical context through associated data.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: AEAD associated data is encrypted and therefore safe for secrets.
questions.explanation: Using a display name or locale-formatted string as associated data makes decryption depend on mutable presentation details and can strand valid ciphertext.

questions.prompt: Which attack can account-bound associated data prevent?
questions.answer: Substituting valid ciphertext from one user, tenant, record type, or purpose into another context.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
